title: wsaw scan result
description: One scan of one target in one consent mode. This schema is wsaw's primary interface: reports, the web interface and CSV exports are all derived views over it. Changes are additive by default; removing or repurposing a field is a breaking change.

schemaVersion.description: Schema version, currently 2.2. 2.2 added bodyCapture and the request payload fields (requestBodyRef and its siblings), additively: a 2.1 document still validates. 2.1 added confidence, additively: a 2.0 document still validates. 2.0 removed environment.warmCache; a 1.x document carries it and no longer validates against this schema.

target.description: Configured target name; stable across scans, which is what ties history together.

consentMode.description: Part of a result's identity. Results are never compared across modes.

termination.description: Why capture stopped. Anything other than idle means the asset list may be incomplete and must not be read as 'nothing was loaded'.

error.description: Set when the scan failed. Its presence invalidates the asset list.

attempt.description: Which attempt of a retried scan produced this result, counting from 1. Absent when retrying is disabled.

attempts.description: How many attempts were allowed for this scan.

previousError.description: Why the attempt before this one failed. Absent on a first attempt.

superseded.description: True on a failed result that a later attempt replaced. The failure remains in the history, but a superseded result is not what the next scan is compared against.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems a reader must see, such as a body that could not be fingerprinted.

storage.description: Web Storage present when the scan finished. A cookie list describes only half of what a site keeps on a visitor's machine.

confidence.description: How far this scan's asset list can be trusted, derived from the rest of this document and from the durations of earlier scans in the same series (Story 5.35). Added in 2.1; absent from a document written before it, which means not computed, never a perfect score.

bodyCapture.description: The body storage this scan ran under, whether it was in the sample, and what it stored (Story 1.11). Added in 2.2; absent from a document written before it, and from a scan that never reached capture. A scan with sampled false stored no body by configuration, which is a different fact from a body that could not be read.

score.description: 100 less every reason's points, clamped at 0, and at most 59 when the differ calls the scan degraded. 100 means every signal was assessed and none fired.

band.description: high is 90-100, medium 60-89, low 1-59. none is a scan that failed or was skipped: no observation, rather than a poor one.

reasons.description: One entry per signal, in a fixed order, including signals that cost nothing and signals that could not be assessed.

medianNs.description: Median duration of the earlier clean scans the duration was compared against.

scans.description: How many earlier scans the median was taken over.

durationReference.description: What the scan's duration was compared against, kept so the score can be checked after those scans are pruned. Absent when there was not enough history; the duration reason then says why.

points.description: How much this signal took off the score.

reference.description: What the observation was compared against, where there is one.

notAssessed.description: Why the signal could not be checked. Its points are then 0.

outcome.description: 'not-needed' means no interaction was required, which is a legitimate and common result, not an error. 'unverified' means the interaction ran but its effect could not be confirmed. 'banner-visible' means the CMP recorded the requested choice but the banner itself was still displayed even after a fallback click was attempted. 'necessary-only' means the requested mode was 'reject' but the banner offered no reject/decline control at all, so wsaw fell back to deselecting every optional category; it is never reported as 'applied' and must not be read as a verified full rejection.

mechanism.description: How the state was reached. A TCF API call is strong evidence; a heuristic label match is weak. A '+click' suffix means the primary mechanism recorded the choice but left the banner displayed, and a fallback click was needed to close it.

heuristic.description: True when the banner was found by guessing at button labels. Such results should be treated with caution.

screenshotsIdentical.description: True when the before- and after-interaction screenshots are byte-for-byte identical, which contradicts an 'applied' outcome and is worth checking even when the outcome is 'banner-visible' or 'failed'.

cmpKind.description: What was found on the page, which is a different question from what the interaction achieved. 'vendor' means a CMP product was identified. 'bespoke' means a consent UI is present and no vendor fingerprint matched it. 'none' means no consent UI was found within the banner wait, and it is the only kind that licenses reading this result as a page that never asks for consent.

bannerHeading.description: The banner's own first line of text, truncated. Page-controlled data, recorded so a reader can tell which banner this was.

consentStorageKeys.description: Web Storage keys written while the interaction ran, as 'local:cookie-accepted'. On a site that keeps consent state outside cookies this is the only trace that the choice was recorded.

staleHostRules.description: Consent rules scoped to this host that did not match it. A host-scoped rule exists because somebody wrote it for this site; its silence usually means the site changed.

diagnostic.description: A banner that was found but not handled: which element matched, what it said, and which controls it offered. Every field is page-controlled text.

userAgent.description: Empty means the browser's own user agent was used.

extraHeaderNames.description: Header names only. Values may be credentials and are never serialized.

browserRuntime.description: "local" when the browser ran as a host process, or the container runtime that ran it. A result is comparable with another only if a reader can see which rendered it.

browserImage.description: Container image, pinned by digest, when the browser ran in a container.

browserSandbox.description: Whether Chrome's own sandbox was active. In a container it depends on the image: the default image turns it off, leaving the container as the only boundary, while an image that declares de.pflege.wsaw.browser.sandbox=enabled (deploy/browser) keeps it, unless a sandbox-weakening switch was passed in browser.container.browserArgs. Either way it is a material fact about the scan.

browserReused.description: True when the browser process had already served another scan, so isolation rested on clearing state rather than on the process boundary.

normalizedUrl.description: The diffing key. Stored so a reader can see exactly what was compared.

phase.description: Whether the request was observed before or after the consent action. A request already in flight keeps the phase it started in.

nonNetwork.description: data:, blob: and similar. Recorded, but nothing left the browser.

beacon.description: A configured rule excluded this request from idle detection: it repeats for as long as the page is open, so the scan recorded it without waiting for it.

bodySha256.description: SHA-256 of the response body, for the resource types in detection.hashResourceTypes only. A body stored for any other type has bodyRef and no digest, so storing more bodies never changes what a comparison sees.

bodyUnavailable.description: Why no digest was taken, or, in a scan that stores bodies, why the body was not stored. A missing digest is always explained rather than silently absent. It starts with a fixed reason — "no body", "body not retrievable", "body larger than the … byte cap", "scan body budget exhausted", "scan ended before the body was read", "body queue full" or "storing the body failed" — optionally followed by ": " and detail.

bodyRef.description: Reference to the stored response body, present when the scan stored bodies. Bodies live outside this document as content-addressed files; fetch one with GET /api/v1/artifacts/{ref}.

bodyIdentity.description: A stable identifier lifted out of the response body by a configured normalize.bodyIdentity rule, such as a tag-manager container version. Present only where a rule matched and the body carried the value. A comparison prefers it over bodySha256, because some scripts rewrite their bytes on every response without changing what they do.

bodyIdentityLabel.description: What bodyIdentity is, for reports, e.g. "GTM container version".

body.description: The stored response body itself. Present only in an export — a HAR, a downloaded result, or the API's result endpoint — and never in the document as stored, which keeps bodies outside it. A result read from the store therefore has bodyRef and no body.

bodyEncoding.description: Present when body is base64-encoded because the bytes are not text. Absent when body is the body as text.

bodyStoredSize.description: How many bytes of the body were kept. Smaller than decodedSize when the size cap truncated it, which is the difference between a short body and a truncated one.

requestBodyRef.description: Reference to the stored request payload — what the page sent, which for a beacon is the data that left the visitor's browser. Present in a sampled scan with bodies.requestBodies on. Added in 2.2.

requestBodySha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored request payload.

requestBodySize.description: Size of the request payload in bytes.

requestBodyMimeType.description: The request's declared content type, the one request header wsaw keeps, because a payload cannot be described without it.

requestBodyUnavailable.description: Why a payload that should have been stored was not. Starts with one of the fixed reasons listed for bodyUnavailable.

requestBodyRedacted.description: A credential wsaw itself supplied (basic auth, an extra header, proxy credentials) was replaced in the payload before it was stored. Nothing the page chose is ever redacted.

requestBody.description: The stored request payload itself, in an export only, exactly like body.

requestBodyEncoding.description: Present when requestBody is base64-encoded because the bytes are not text.

valueSha256.description: Cookie values are fingerprinted, never stored: they routinely contain identifiers.
Values are fingerprinted, never stored: they carry identifiers as routinely as cookie values do.

store.description: Which bodies a sampled scan keeps: none, those of detection.hashResourceTypes (hashed), or every network request's (all).

ratio.description: Configured share of scans that store bodies, from 0 to 1.

ratioWindowNs.description: Timespan the ratio is honoured over, in nanoseconds.

requestBodies.description: Whether request payloads are stored too.

forced.description: The sample was forced for this scan (wsaw scan --bodies), regardless of the ratio.

decision.description: Why the scan was or was not sampled. ledger-unavailable means the sampling ledger could not be read, so the ratio could not be honoured and nothing was stored; storage-disabled-by-reload means a retry inherited a sampled decision after a reload turned storage off.

decidedBy.description: Scan ID of the attempt that took the decision. A retry inherits its first attempt's decision, so on a retry this names an earlier scan.

windowScans.description: Scans of this series in the trailing window when the decision was taken, this one included.

windowSampled.description: How many of windowScans were sampled, this one included if it was.

maxBodyBytes.description: Per-body cap the scan stored under.

maxScanBytes.description: Cap on all bodies one scan may store.

bodiesUnavailable.description: Requests whose body or payload a sampled scan could not store, each with its reason on the request.

budgetExhausted.description: The scan reached maxScanBytes; later bodies are recorded as unavailable for that reason.
